<p>One of the most common and concerning diagnoses women hear in the doctor's office during pregnancy is <strong>"Uterine tone"</strong> or <strong>"Hypertonus."</strong> When a doctor frowns during an ultrasound and says, "You have tone," it becomes an alarm signal for many expectant mothers.</p><p>But what actually is this "tone"? Does every abdominal tightening result in a miscarriage? Or is it a natural reaction of the body? Let's explore the truths, myths, and medical facts behind this popular diagnosis.</p><h2>What is uterine tone, actually?</h2><p>In simple terms, the uterus (womb) is a hollow, muscular organ. Like every muscle (for example, a representative arm muscle), the uterus has the ability to contract and relax.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Normal Tone:</strong> It is normal for the uterine muscle to be under slight tension.</p></li><li><p><strong>Hypertonus (High Tone):</strong> This is the premature, involuntary, and prolonged contraction of the uterine muscles.</p></li></ul><p></p><p>Throughout pregnancy, as the uterus grows, the muscle fibers stretch. Sometimes, the uterus may contract for a short period while walking, laughing, or when the fetus moves. This is a natural occurrence. However, if these contractions are painful and last a long time, one should be careful.</p><h2>Symptoms: How can you feel the tone?</h2><p>Many women describe tone as "turning to stone."</p><ul><li><p><strong>Abdominal hardening:</strong> When you place your hand on your stomach, you feel it is as hard as a rock.</p></li><li><p><strong>Pain:</strong> Dull or pulling pains similar to menstrual cramps, starting from the lower back and radiating to the lower abdomen.</p></li><li><p><strong>Feeling of heaviness:</strong> A sense of pressure or fullness in the groin area.</p></li></ul><h2>Why does it occur? (Causes)</h2><p>Many factors can cause hypertonus:</p><ul><li><p><strong>Progesterone deficiency:</strong> A lack of this hormone, which protects the pregnancy, can prevent the uterus from relaxing.</p></li><li><p><strong>Magnesium deficiency:</strong> Magnesium is essential for muscle relaxation.</p></li><li><p><strong>Stress and fatigue:</strong> Nervous tension directly affects the muscles.</p></li><li><p><strong>Physical exertion:</strong> Lifting heavy objects or standing for long periods.</p></li><li><p><strong>Infections:</strong> Sexually transmitted infections or kidney problems.</p></li><li><p><strong>Gas and bloating:</strong> Intestinal problems can create tone by putting pressure on the uterus.</p></li></ul><p></p><h2>When is tone dangerous?</h2><p>Not every abdominal tightening is scary. However, in the following cases, it can create a risk of <strong>miscarriage</strong> or <strong>preterm labor</strong>:</p><ul><li><p><strong>In the early weeks (1st trimester):</strong> Tone accompanied by severe pain or spotting can cause the embryo to detach from the uterine wall (hematoma).</p></li><li><p><strong>In later weeks:</strong> If contractions become regular and do not subside with rest, this can lead to shortening of the cervix and premature birth.</p></li></ul><p></p><blockquote><p>Don't Mistake It for Braxton Hicks (False Labor)!</p></blockquote><p>Painless, irregular, and short-lived (30-60 seconds) contractions starting after the 20th week are "false labor." This is the uterus practicing for birth and is completely normal.</p><p>&gt;</p><h2>Treatment and First Aid: What to do?</h2><p>If you feel tension in your abdomen, do not panic immediately. Stress increases tone even further.</p><h3>First Aid at Home (Before the doctor)</h3><ul><li><p><strong>Lie down and rest:</strong> Stop moving and take a comfortable position.</p></li><li><p><strong>Drink water:</strong> Dehydration is one of the main causes of muscle spasms. Drink 1-2 glasses of water.</p></li><li><p><strong>Take deep breaths:</strong> Inhale deeply through your nose and exhale slowly through your mouth. This relaxes the body.</p></li><li><p><strong>Warm shower:</strong> Warm water (not hot!) can soften the muscles.</p></li></ul><h3>Medical Treatment (Only with a doctor's prescription!)</h3><p>In Azerbaijan, doctors usually prescribe the following agents during hypertonus:</p><ul><li><p><strong>Magnesium B6:</strong> To calm the muscles and strengthen the nervous system.</p></li><li><p><strong>Spasmolytics (Papaverine suppositories, No-spa):</strong> "Emergency" tools to eliminate pain and spasms.</p></li><li><p><strong>Progesterone preparations (Duphaston, Utrogestan):</strong> If the cause is hormonal deficiency.</p></li></ul><p></p><blockquote><p>Attention: Do not take any medication, even vitamins, without consulting your doctor.</p></blockquote><p>&gt;</p><p>The diagnosis of "uterine tone" should not scare you, but it should not be ignored either. Listen to your body. If your pains are severe, if there is bleeding, or if you are simply worried, be sure to contact your doctor.</p><p>For your pregnancy to pass calmly and without stress, record your daily symptoms in the <strong>Anacan app</strong> and benefit from the advice in the "Safety" section. Remember, a calm mother means a healthy baby.</p>
